speaker: Doctor
text: I need to understand the timing of your symptoms; do your double vision and weakness occur simultaneously or at different times? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel.

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating double vision, symmetrical proximal weakness (difficulty climbing stairs), and distal weakness in the absence of fever or family history strongly suggests an autoimmune neuromuscular junction disorder.
